content.title: About
content.content: Oat squares are crunchy cereal pieces made from whole oat groats, typically shaped as squares. They are produced from whole oats, sugar, salt, and sometimes added ingredients such as dried fruit or nuts. The product is often enjoyed as a quick breakfast or snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oat squares are commonly called “oat squares” in Russia and other CIS countries.
Oats, the base ingredient, are one of the oldest cultivated grains.
Unlike many breakfast cereals, oat squares usually contain no artificial flavors.
Oats are rich in beta‑glucan, a soluble fiber that supports heart health.
Some versions are fortified with B‑vitamins and iron.

items.title: Rich in beta‑glucan
items.content: Beta‑glucan helps lower cholesterol levels and supports the immune system.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs provide sustained energy and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and helps regulate blood sugar.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 are involved in carbohydrate metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other dry cereals, oat squares have a modest fat content.

items.title: Oat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to oats or to added ingredients such as nuts.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Certain varieties contain added sugar, which should be considered by people with diabetes or low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Oats are often processed on equipment that also handles gluten; those with celiac disease should choose certified gluten‑free oat squares.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Oat squares can be eaten dry, added to milk, yogurt, or kefir. They are also used in granola mixes, desserts, and energy bars. For a softer texture, pour hot milk over them and let them sit for a few minutes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, keep in the refrigerator to prevent moisture and spoilage.
